words.technical: Gold's trend score is clearly negative at about -1.06, and all four lookback windows (21, 63, 126 and 252 days) agree, with the 63-day window weakest. The price sits in the bottom tenth of its 252-day range, so the 4.4% bounce this week left it near the low end of the year's range. Daily volatility is about 2.2%, which sets the width of next week's range. The trend reading is why the stance is Wait rather than Flat.
words.macro: Gold broke below $3,500 during the Thanksgiving-shortened week before easing into the weekend just above $3,650 per ounce. Selling intensified on Wednesday after October PCE inflation rose 3.8% annually, strengthening expectations that the Fed would raise rates again in December. Markets stayed heavily tilted toward another Fed rate increase, with the dollar comparatively firm and pressuring gold.
words.long_term: Gold sits near the bottom of its year's range, yet the 252-day trend reading is only mildly negative, so the structural picture is a pullback rather than a collapse. The path from here is tied to the Fed's rate path and the dollar.

eoy_scenarios.central: Gold finishes the year inside the central band of roughly 3,510 to 4,020, with the Fed's December decision and the November inflation prints setting the pace but neither forcing a break.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Gold rises above 4,020 if inflation data soften enough to cool rate-increase expectations and the dollar loses its bid, drawing back the buyers who stepped away during this month's selling.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Gold falls below 3,510 if rate-increase expectations harden further and the dollar stays firm, extending the pressure that took it to this month's lows.

words.technical: Silver's trend score is about -1.21, negative in every lookback window and weakest over 63 days. The price is in the bottom 5% of its 252-day range, so the 6.5% rebound this week is small against the damage already done. Daily volatility of about 4.1% is roughly double gold's, which is why its percentage range is the widest in the set.
words.macro: Silver was quoted at $42.27, up 1.12%. Traders leaned heavily toward another Fed rate increase, and reduced holiday liquidity could amplify price movements.
words.long_term: Silver trades with gold's rate and dollar drivers but with about twice the volatility, so the structural picture is the same pullback delivered in larger swings. A durable recovery needs gold to stabilise first.

eoy_scenarios.central: Silver ends the year between roughly 38.94 and 50.97, moving with gold and with the rate path rather than on industrial news.

eoy_scenarios.downside: Silver drops below 38.94 if gold resumes falling and the dollar holds firm, with thin year-end liquidity adding to the swings.

words.technical: Oil's trend score is only mildly negative at about -0.25 because the windows disagree: the 21-day reading is sharply negative while the 252-day reading is still positive. The price sits near the middle of its 252-day range, with daily volatility of about 2.9%. A mixed trend with no extreme in range position is why the stance is Flat, the stance that expects the week to close inside the published range.
words.macro: Crude prices fell to around $83 per barrel on Friday. Brent rose about 3.1 per cent across the week, its first weekly gain of November, after a projectile struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Thursday. OPEC+ ministers meet online on Sunday, November 29, and are set to keep first-quarter 2027 output targets unchanged.
words.long_term: Oil is in a mid-range holding pattern after this month's sell-off, with the price set by Gulf supply security and producer-group quota decisions more than by demand. The longer trend is still positive.

eoy_scenarios.central: WTI finishes the year in the central band of roughly 76 to 91.5, with the producer group's quotas unchanged and Gulf shipping largely intact.
eoy_scenarios.upside: WTI rises above 91.5 if attacks on tankers or Saudi facilities escalate into real supply loss, or if the producer group tightens output.
eoy_scenarios.downside: WTI falls below 76 if Gulf shipments keep recovering and demand softens, extending the month's sell-off into year-end.

words.technical: Bitcoin's trend score is about -1.26, driven by very negative 21-day and 63-day readings of about -2.1 each, while the 126-day and 252-day readings are only mildly negative. The price is in the bottom 6% of its 252-day range, so the 2.2% gain this week is a bounce off the lows. Daily volatility of about 2.4% is the basis of next week's range, which runs from about 56,100 to 65,100.
words.macro: Bitcoin fell 26.3% over the month to November 27, closing just below $60,000. November withdrawals from spot Bitcoin ETFs reached $5.78 billion. November is already the worst month for spot Bitcoin ETFs since their January 2024 launch. Spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their withdrawal streak to seven sessions by November 26.
words.long_term: Bitcoin has dropped from the middle of its yearly range to near the bottom within weeks, and the long-run trend readings have turned negative. Flows into and out of spot funds are currently the clearest sign of marginal demand.

eoy_scenarios.central: Bitcoin ends the year between roughly 56,400 and 67,300, stabilising as fund outflows slow without a clear return of buyers.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Bitcoin rises above 67,300 if the record fund outflows reverse into inflows and risk appetite from the equity rally carries over.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Bitcoin falls below 56,400 if fund outflows continue at November's pace and a break of the recent lows forces further selling.

words.technical: The dollar index has the strongest positive trend in the set, with a score of about +1.26 and all four lookback windows positive. The price is in the top 4% of its 252-day range, with very low daily volatility of about 0.34%, so even small moves matter for next week's narrow range. words.macro: The dollar index gained 0.36% to 104.035. The US 10-year yield rose to 4.936%. The DXY was pinned around 103.75, below 104.00 resistance, after retreating from 20-month highs at 104.53.
words.long_term: The dollar is near 20-month highs, supported by a Fed that markets expect to raise rates. Because it sits near the top of its range, the risk is a reversal if rate expectations soften.

eoy_scenarios.central: The dollar index ends the year between roughly 102.96 and 105.29, with the Fed's December decision largely priced in.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The dollar index rises above 105.29 if the Fed raises rates and signals more, and inflation data keep yields climbing.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The dollar index falls below 102.96 if the Fed disappoints rate-increase expectations or payrolls come in weak enough to pull yields lower.

week_summary: Equities led a sharp rebound in a holiday-shortened week, with the Nasdaq 100 up more than 6%, while precious metals bounced from lows and bitcoin stayed near 60,000. The dollar index kept its high range position as markets leaned toward a Fed rate increase on 9 December. Five of seven instruments carry a Wait or Hold stance because the shorter trends have not turned despite the bounces; oil is Flat, and the S&P 500 is a No read ahead of the payrolls report.
